## Summary

FLA causal-LM heads share logits selection and shifted-label loss, and accept `num_items_in_batch` for token-normalized training. This is layer 3 of native stack #1504, following #1503 and #1500. Existing fusion choices, custom criteria, L2 regularization, checkpoint paths, and MoM's `num_logits_to_keep` argument are preserved; MoM also accepts `logits_to_keep`.

With labels, heads project the full sequence for loss, fixing CAT's shape mismatch when `logits_to_keep` is set. MoM returns logits without labels even when its training-time fused-loss option is enabled. Packed-label boundary handling remains in #1454.

## Test plan

Tested source revision: `a6bdd67dddc929ed883fc215d3a6265d0871a660`; ancestry-only integration of merged prerequisites preserves this tree.

- GB200, PyTorch 2.11.0.post1+cu132.msh, strict `FLA_CI_ENV=0 FLA_DISABLE_BACKEND_DISPATCH=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4`, Transformers 5.6.2: `python -m pytest tests/models/test_cache.py tests/models/test_generation_utils.py tests/models/test_transformers.py tests/models/test_causal_lm_loss.py tests/layers/test_preconditioned_cache.py -q --tb=short`: **173 passed, 1 skipped**. RWKV7 initialization needs missing CPU LAPACK. Fused/unfused loss and gradients match references; cases cover normalization, L2 options, custom criteria without mutation, both MoM logits names, integer/tensor selection, cache and checkpoint behavior.
- Same targets on CPU with Transformers 5.20.1: **151 passed, 23 skipped**; accelerator-only and LAPACK-dependent cases are identified as skips. Minimum/current Transformers 5.x model API and split-package checks pass in [CPU CI](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/actions/runs/39042824095).
- All 40 head callsites were audited, including inherited StickBreaking attention, RWKV7 shifted labels, MoM auxiliary loss and model-specific fusion choices. Existing positional argument order is preserved.
- Seven-family GPU integration: **29 passed, 18 skipped, 4 failed**, matching the limitations documented in #1503: three LAPACK-dependent RWKV7 cases and a baseline-reproduced PrecondKDA dense/packed failure. With identical weights/inputs, all 108 PrecondKDA output/gradient tensors match baseline bitwise. Both preconditioned long-generation checks pass. This broad matrix is not claimed green; the changed loss/API gates pass.
- Running the general model files before the preconditioned files additionally reproduces the baseline naive-preconditioner failure: **28 passed, 18 skipped, 5 failed**. Test ordering changes random initialization; the fixed-weight replay above separates these existing failures from the cache/API refactor.
- Pre-commit, header/lint CI, and `git diff --check` pass. Numerical tolerances were not changed.

## Benchmark / NCU

GB200, PyTorch 2.11.0.post1+cu132.msh, Transformers 5.6.2, strict flags above; baseline `dcfd8700`, candidate `a6bdd67d`. Isolated GLA embedding/norm/head training step with zero decoder layers, B=2, T=128, H=128, V=4096, bf16, dense inputs, `fuse_norm=False`, mean loss. Each step zeros gradients, runs forward and backward; 10 warmups, then median of five synchronized 50-step samples.

| Loss path | Before (ms) | After (ms) | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unfused | 0.722 | 0.750 | +3.9% |
| Fused CE | 1.071 | 1.105 | +3.2% |
| Fused linear + CE | 3.558 | 3.764 | +5.8% |

All three paths are slightly slower in this sample; no speedup or performance-neutrality claim is made. These are small head-path measurements, not end-to-end training throughput. Packed-label correctness/performance remains external in #1454. No kernels changed; NCU is not applicable.

pr_branch_commits.author: mikasenghaas
pr_branch_commits.message:
Pass the wire format to replay views

A client can rewrite a replayed turn differently per wire format:
pi and OpenCode drop whitespace-only assistant text over Anthropic
messages but keep it over Responses. Give each dialect a name, record
the one the harness speaks on the trace, and pass it to
`Harness.replay_view`.

Scope pi's view to the formats that drop the text, and add views for
OpenCode (Anthropic messages) and Kimi Code (every format). A new
integration test runs every transport a harness config can select
and asserts one branch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

pr_branch_commits.message:
Carry the dialect on each request, not the trace

The trace-wide dialect let one request overwrite it while another was
suspended, so the second request matched its prompt (and committed
its turn) under the wrong replay view. Each PendingTurn now keeps its
request's dialect, and the trace keeps one head index per dialect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

A dialect-blind view either misses the rewrite or claims one the client never makes. - A new `DialectName` Literal in `verifiers/v1/types.py` defines the wire formats once: `chat_completions`, `responses`, `anthropic_messages`. Each dialect has a `name` of that type, and the `transport` settings of pi, opencode and kimi-code use it. - The interception server passes each request's dialect to `graph.prepare_turn`. The `PendingTurn` keeps it through `commit`, so overlapping requests in different dialects each match under their own view. The trace keeps one node index per dialect, and every new node goes into each index that exists. - `Harness.replay_view(message, dialect: DialectName | None)` receives that name. The graph passes it when it matches a replayed turn to its sampled node. - Replay views: - **pi:** only `chat_completions` and `anthropic_messages` ([completions](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.86.1/packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts#L1290), [anthropic](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.86.1/packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts#L1315)). Its Responses adapter keeps the text. - **opencode:** new view, only `anthropic_messages` ([source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.0.26/packages/ai/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts#L929)). - **kimi-code:** new view, every dialect.
